evidence: Earlier induced-forest rook result forbids bipartite cycles, but the present three-independent rook sets permit alternating cycles and three-stars; neither polynomial determines the other by a simple parameter renaming.
Cabrera-Martínez et al. study total outer k-independent domination in general; their inequalities do not count all complements of three-independent rook sets.
Mao et al. provide a nonsharp general upper bound for balanced complete factors, whereas the present equality is a sharp two-factor classification.

value.rationale: Closes a natural complete-product k-independence counting problem and sharpens square maximum from literature bounds to 2q, with all maxima bijective to spanning bipartite two-factors; also determines total outer three-independent domination polynomial and optimal multiplicities on an infinite range. This is a natural motivated all-set classification, not a trivial numeric recomputation.
